long_description: Pear Therapeutics pioneered prescription digital therapeutics (PDTs), becoming the first company to receive FDA approval for a mobile app treating substance use disorders when reSET was cleared in 2017. The company developed reSET for general substance use disorder, reSET-O for opioid use disorder, and Somryst for chronic insomnia - all using cognitive behavioral therapy techniques. Despite raising over $400 million and significant clinical validation, Pear filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in April 2023, citing slow reimbursement adoption and high costs. The company laid off 90%+ of employees and ceased accepting new prescriptions. In December 2023, PursueCare acquired reSET and reSET-O, now offering them for $90 out of pocket. Nox Health Group acquired Somryst. The products remain available to patients through their new owners.

faqs.a: Pear Therapeutics filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in April 2023, citing slow reimbursement adoption and high costs. The company laid off 90%+ of employees. PursueCare acquired reSET and reSET-O in December 2023; Nox Health Group acquired Somryst.

faqs.q: Are reSET and Somryst still available?
faqs.a: Yes. PursueCare now offers reSET and reSET-O for $90 out of pocket. Somryst is available through Nox Health Group. Both products retain their FDA clearance.

faqs.q: Was reSET the first FDA-approved digital therapeutic?
faqs.a: Yes, reSET received FDA De Novo clearance in 2017, becoming the first FDA-approved mobile app for treating substance use disorders.
Despite raising $400M+ and achieving FDA clearance, Pear struggled with slow reimbursement adoption, high costs, and lower-than-expected revenue ($12.7M in 2022 vs. $22M projected).
